hook.text: A 30-meter tube of mud from the ocean floor can tell the story of 5 million years of climate.

buildup.text: Scientists drill sediment cores from research ships, extracting cylinders of layered seafloor deposits.

discovery.text: Each layer records past conditions—temperature, ice volume, productivity—from the shells trapped inside.

twist.text: Oxygen isotopes in foraminifera shells reveal whether ice sheets were growing or melting when they lived.

climax.text: Sediment cores proved that ice ages cycle every 100,000 years—matching Earth's orbital variations.

punchline.text: Mud remembers what the sky has forgotten.

quiz.question: What do oxygen isotopes in sediment cores reveal?
options: Past ice sheet size and ocean temperature
